The contract in `src/parse.ts` needed no new code. The spec says there are no new exports and every signature stays the same. The file already exports everything the scenarios use: `parseURL`, `parsePath`, `parseAuth`, `parseHost`, `stringifyParsedURL`, `parseFilename`, `ParsedURL`, `ParsedAuth` and `ParsedHost`. All of them are unchanged, with their bodies exactly as they were.

The only edit is a few lines added to `parseURL`'s doc comment. They state the new rule in the spec's words: the drive-letter slash is removed only when the protocol is written exactly as `file:`, and every other URL keeps its pathname as written. The `parseURL` code itself still has the old behaviour, so changing it is the implementer's job.

The type check reports no errors, and the existing suite passes: 13 files, 467 tests. Only `src/parse.ts` was modified.

Exported names added: none.

I wrote the test suite in `test/ufo-drive-letters-confirmed.test.ts`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors, and the file also type-checks on its own (that config only covers `src`).

**The tests don't all fail, contrary to what you expected.** `src/parse.ts` doesn't throw `not implemented`: the uncommitted diff only adds a doc comment, and `parseURL` still has its old code. So right now 14 tests fail and 30 pass:
- **Failing (14):** the new behaviour. Non-file URLs keep `/C:/x`; `FILE:` and `File:` don't count as `file:`; same for `defaultProto` `"FILE://"` and `"http://"`, protocol-relative URLs and `files:`; plus the round-trip cases and one `parseFilename` case.
- **Passing (30):** behaviour the spec says stays the same, such as drive-letter handling for `file:` URLs and inputs without a protocol.

**What's covered:**
- Every scenario has a test, keyed `[happy-1]`–`[happy-7]`, `[boundary-1]`–`[boundary-10]` and `[unhappy-1]`. Scenario outlines get one test per example row.
- For happy scenarios with a single example, I added one boundary test that follows directly from the spec, mostly the bare-drive-letter form `/C:`. For example, `parseFilename("https://e.com/C:", { strict: false })` must return `"C:"`; the old code returns `undefined`.
- I used the same style as `test/parse.test.ts`: results compared with `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`, and flat top-level tests generated from tables by loops, with no `describe`. The `[protocolRelative]` flag is read with `Symbol.for("ufo:protocolRelative")`, since it isn't exported.
- I ran prettier on the file because the repo's lint step checks `test/`. Nothing else in the repo was changed.

44 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `test/hidden-ufo-drive-letters-confirmed/parse-drive-letters.test.ts`. It passes against a reference implementation that follows the spec, and every test fails when `parseURL` throws `not implemented`.

**One rule isn't met as the folder stands now:** `parseURL` in `src/parse.ts` doesn't throw `not implemented`. It still has the original body, and only its doc comment was changed. Against that code, 60 of the 154 tests fail and 94 pass. The ones that pass are the cases where the old and new behaviour agree, such as `file:///C:/x` → `C:/x`, the drive-letter-host case and the `stringifyParsedURL` results. To check the rule, I ran the suite in a copy of the repo in the scratchpad with a throwing stub in place of `parseURL`, and all 154 tests failed. Nothing in the real repo was changed apart from the new test file.

**Checks:**
- **Reference implementation** (a scratch copy where the slash is removed only when `protocol === "file:"`): all 154 pass. This run caught one wrong expected value of mine, which I've fixed (`?a=1&b=/D:` becomes `?a=1&b=D:`).
- **Type check:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. That config only covers `src`, so I also type-checked the test file on its own with `--skipLibCheck`, which was clean. Without that flag, the only errors come from vite's type files in `node_modules`, not from the test file.

**What it covers:**
- Every spec scenario row, keyed `[happy-1..7]`, `[boundary-1..10]` and `[unhappy-1]`.
- Extra inputs for each public test. Each group has a comment naming the public test it extends.
- Cases aimed at shortcuts that would pass the public suite:
  - **Protocol check:**
    - Leading-whitespace handling: `trim()` or skipping one character (tab, newline and mixed `\0`/space runs).
    - Matching `file` loosely: case-insensitive matching (`fILE:`, `filE:`), or `includes`/`startsWith` (`xfile:`, `file+ssh:`, `file.x:`, `fil:`).
  - **`defaultProto`:**
    - Taking it into account when the input already has a protocol (`http://…` with `"file://"`).
    - Treating `"//"` as anything but protocol-relative, which keeps the slash.
  - **Drive-letter match:**
    - Character-class mistakes: `[A-z]` (`_`, `` ` ``, `[`, `^`) and `/[a-z]/iu` (the Kelvin sign and long s).
    - Replacing every match instead of the first, or only matching at the start of the path (later segments, search, hash, `file://///C:`).
  - **Non-file URLs:** keeping a fixed list of protocols that skip normalization (`ws:`, `s3:`, `custom-proto:`).
  - **`parseFilename`:** on `http://e.com/C:.txt` it returns `C:.txt` under the spec, but `undefined` with the old pathname.

154 tests in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
